unanticipated_findings: Log injection / log forging via PATH_INFO. src/webhookd/app.py:105 logs the rejection with `log.warning("rejected %s %s: %s (%s)", method, path, exc.code, exc.detail)` and src/webhookd/app.py:136 embeds the raw path in the detail; neither is escaped or repr'd. PATH_INFO is URL-decoded by the server, so a percent-encoded newline lands verbatim in the log file. Reproduce: with the service running, `curl -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8125/hooks/%0a2026-08-07%2000:00:00%20INFO%20%20%20%20webhookd.http:%20accepted%20sender=acme%20FORGED'`. The log then contains a fabricated line `2026-08-07 00:00:00 INFO    webhookd.http: accepted sender=acme FORGED` that is indistinguishable from a real one. Unauthenticated (routing happens before signature verification) and it is the one attacker-controlled string on the reject path that is not repr'd — the timestamp and signature details are (signatures.py:279, :283). Impact is on log integrity/forensics, not on delivery correctness.

README port advice breaks the very next commands it shows. README.md:31 offers `webhookd serve --port 8123` when 8080 is taken, but `webhookd send` computes its target from `config.server.port` (src/webhookd/cli.py:112), not from the serve override, and only `serve` has a `--port` flag (cli.py:243 vs cli.py:249-259). Following the README literally after a port clash gives a failure against whatever else is on 8080 rather than a hint; you must know to pass `--url http://127.0.0.1:8123`, which the quick-start never mentions. I hit this on a machine where 8080 was already bound by an unrelated process. The primary path (default port free) works exactly as documented.
Minor doc drift: README.md:24 says `pytest # 241 tests, no network needed`; the suite is now 243 tests.

`webhookd replay <id>` reports success on a delivery it cannot actually rescue when the handler is still failing, which is expected, but the CLI's message (`delivery 1 queued for reprocessing`, cli.py:188) is printed unconditionally even though `store.requeue` returns a boolean that is discarded (cli.py:187). The prior `store.get` check makes this benign today, but the return value being dropped means a future concurrent-delete race would silently report success.

Not a defect, but worth recording as design context for the duplicate guarantee: `Dispatcher._process` calls `store.mark_done` without re-checking that its lease is still held (src/webhookd/dispatcher.py:154, store.py:214-224). A handler that outruns `lease_seconds` (default 300s) can therefore be running concurrently with a second worker that reclaimed the same row. The README (lines 111-128) and store.py:1-23 both state this at-least-once floor explicitly and tell handlers to be idempotent, and `event.attempt` flags the repeat, so it is disclosed rather than hidden.
